practiceableQuestions.promptText: The line graph below shows the percentage of households owning zero, one, or two or more cars in a European country between 1980 and 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
practiceableQuestions.sourceName: LumaReader Original Academic Bank (Inspired by public topic index)
practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: Some people believe that governments should invest heavily in public transport rather than building new roads for private cars. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
practiceableQuestions.notes: Original dataset & prompt; each year sums to 100% across household car-ownership tiers.

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The pie chart below illustrates the average proportion of monthly household expenditure across six categories in a coastal city in 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: In many countries, the cost of living is rising rapidly. What are the primary causes of this trend, and what measures can individuals and governments take to address it?
practiceableQuestions.notes: Original pie chart dataset; slice percentages sum to exactly 100.0%.

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The two maps below show an island before and after the construction of tourist facilities. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

afterFeatures.label: Reception block and restaurant connected by vehicle track
Two clusters of guest huts connected by footpaths
Boat pier extending into southern bay

practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: Developing remote natural areas for international tourism brings economic benefits, but it often damages the local environment. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
practiceableQuestions.notes: Original vector map specification with verified before/after spatial features.

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The diagram below shows the stages involved in the dry-method production of roasted coffee beans from harvesting to commercial packaging. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

processSteps.title: Hand Picking
processSteps.detail: Ripe red coffee cherries are harvested by hand from coffee trees.

processSteps.title: Sun Drying & Sorting
processSteps.detail: Cherries are spread on patios under the sun for 2–3 weeks and raked regularly.

processSteps.title: Mechanical Hulling
processSteps.detail: Dried outer skins and parchment layers are removed in a milling machine.

processSteps.title: Grading & Screening
processSteps.detail: Green beans are sorted by size, weight, and color defects.

processSteps.title: Thermal Roasting
processSteps.detail: Beans are roasted at 200°C–220°C in rotating drums to develop aroma.

processSteps.title: Cooling, Grinding & Vacuum Packing
processSteps.detail: Roasted beans are air-cooled, optionally ground, and sealed into valve bags.

practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: Modern automated manufacturing has reduced the price of everyday consumer goods, yet many traditional skills are disappearing. Do the advantages of automation outweigh the disadvantages?
practiceableQuestions.notes: Original 6-step process diagram with verified sequential step connectivity.

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The bar chart below compares annual visitor numbers (in thousands) across four public museums in a capital city in 2015, 2020, and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: Some people think that all public museums and art galleries should be free of charge, while others believe visitors should pay an admission fee. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
practiceableQuestions.notes: Original bar chart dataset with 4 museums across 3 benchmark years.

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The table below gives data on the population distribution (in millions) across three age brackets in four regions in 2025, along with total regional populations. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: In many countries, the proportion of older people is steadily increasing. Does this demographic shift bring more positive or negative effects to society?
practiceableQuestions.notes: Original table dataset; row totals (15.0, 10.5, 17.0, 5.5) match exact series sums.

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The bar chart below shows the average residential property price (in thousand USD) for apartments, townhouses, and detached homes in three cities in 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: In many major cities, young adults find it increasingly difficult to purchase their first home. What are the reasons for this, and how can governments help?

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The pie chart below shows the breakdown of municipal freshwater consumption across five sectors in an Australian metropolitan region in 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: Fresh water is becoming a scarce resource in many parts of the world. What are the causes of water scarcity, and what steps should be taken to conserve water?
practiceableQuestions.notes: Original pie chart dataset; slice percentages sum to exactly 100.0%.

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The line graph below illustrates the urban population growth (in millions) of three Asian metropolitan areas from 1990 to 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: Rapid urbanization creates severe housing and traffic pressures in large cities. What problems does overpopulation in cities cause, and how can they be solved?

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The two plans below show a municipal community park in 1995 and its redesigned layout in 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

beforeFeatures.label: Two wooden benches along gravel path

afterFeatures.label: Expanded wetland pond with wooden viewing deck
Children's playground and outdoor fitness zone
Community cafe and cycle racks near North entrance
Accessible paved loop trail and solar lighting

practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: Public parks and green spaces are essential for urban residents' physical and mental wellbeing. How can city planners balance green spaces with the need for commercial and residential buildings?
practiceableQuestions.notes: Original municipal park before/after map comparison.

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The diagram below illustrates the closed-loop industrial process for recycling end-of-life photovoltaic solar panels into purified raw materials. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

processSteps.title: Collection & Frame Dismantling
processSteps.detail: Used solar panels are collected and aluminum frames plus junction boxes are detached mechanically.

processSteps.title: Thermal Delamination
processSteps.detail: Panels pass through a 500°C furnace to evaporate the encapsulating polymer layer.

processSteps.title: Optical Glass Separation
processSteps.detail: Clean glass cullet (95% recovery) is separated on vibrating conveyors for glass remanufacturing.

processSteps.title: Chemical Etching & Metal Leaching
processSteps.detail: Silicon cells undergo acid leaching to extract silver, copper, and tin.

processSteps.title: Wafer Ingot Recasting
processSteps.detail: Purified silicon is melted and cast into new solar-grade ingots for new PV modules.

practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: While renewable energy technologies reduce carbon emissions, their manufacturing and disposal also create environmental challenges. To what extent should manufacturers be legally responsible for recycling their products?

practiceableQuestions.promptText: The line graph below shows renewable electricity generation (in terawatt-hours) from wind, solar, and hydro in a Nordic country from 2010 to 2025, while the pie chart shows the share of grid battery storage capacity by sector in 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
practiceableQuestions.companionTask2Prompt: Some people argue that transitioning completely to renewable energy is too expensive for developing economies. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
practiceableQuestions.notes: Original combined line graph + pie chart dataset; pie slices sum to 100.0%.
